Ask only when both sides changed the same logic and picking either loses behavior.

2. **CI red** → find out whether the failure is this PR's. It isn't if it is red on the base branch too, or names a service the diff doesn't touch and reproduces on one re-run. Any other failure is yours to root-cause and fix; "flake" is not a root cause, and a cause that turns out to lie outside this change is handled as above. Never skip, disable, or quarantine a test to get green; never push an empty commit or close and reopen the PR to kick CI. Green has to mean this code passed its tests, and none of those shows that.

3. **Review comments** → do a human reviewer's small, local asks (nits, renames, an added test, a one-function refactor) and lint-bot fixes, and push. An ask you can't size is large. On a PR you did not open, answer a larger ask (multi-file refactor, API or schema change, open-ended design feedback) with a proposal and never push or resolve: the author decides. On a PR you only watch, or when the author is your user, make the proposal to your user.

A bot finding is a claim to verify, not an order. Trace a realistic path to the failure and weigh the code a fix adds against what it prevents: fix what is real and in proportion; otherwise answer its thread with what you traced and put the call to your user, whose answer holds for later PRs too. A red-circle comment is never optional, whatever its wording or a skill says, and neither is a failing Claude Approvals row.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

I've sent the analyst a correction. The rule stays a reporting requirement on tooling PRs. A real addition that closes a defect should be recommended as one, and a deletion offered alongside it only if one exists.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""scripts/audit/supersession_backpointer_audit.py — currency lives at the superseded text.

WHY THIS EXISTS (RC3, DR-2026-09-26-recurring-defect-shapes-remediation.md section 4).
Binding text lives in more than five stores (DRs, the append-only ledger, the YAML
register, the `decisions` table, CLAUDE.md, the research contract and its SessionStart
copy, code comments, `sessions/*.md`), and a ruling superseding one of them was sometimes
left with no local mark: a reader who reaches the superseded sentence by grep meets it
with nothing saying it no longer holds. The fix is not a currency INDEX — that would be
the next store rule 5 forbids — it is a pointer at the text itself, anchored on quotes
that occur exactly once at both ends, checked with plain file I/O so `.ignore` cannot
hide the target (owner rulings live overwhelmingly in `sessions/`, which `.ignore` hides
from ripgrep and the Grep tool).

THE GRAMMAR, read from the ledger and from any DR using the same trailer:

    SUPERSEDES: <target path> :: "<verbatim quote from the target>"
      BY: references/project-standards.md :: "<verbatim quote from the superseding ruling>"

NORMALISATION (so a quote survives comment wrapping, YAML folding and Markdown
blockquotes): for each line, strip leading whitespace and one leading run of `#`, `>`,
`//` or `--`, join the lines with spaces, and collapse whitespace. Both quotes must
occur EXACTLY ONCE in their own file under this normalisation.

FAILS when: the target quote occurs 0 times (edited in place, which the append-not-edit
practice forbids) or more than once (ambiguous); the BY quote does not occur exactly
once in the ledger; or no line in the target quote's own paragraph, or in the paragraph
or blockquote immediately after it, both names SUPERSEDED or AMENDED and carries the BY
quote verbatim. `BY` is always required — `DATE:` lines in the ledger are not unique
(the most repeated closes thirteen entries), so a marker cannot be anchored on one.

EXAMINED counts `SUPERSEDES:` lines. Today there may be none in a fresh clone before the
first seed lands — that is NOTHING-IN-SCOPE, not a failure (CLAUDE.md section 5a): a
check with no subject must say so, not pass by finding nothing to check.
"""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "scripts"))
import dbcore                                                        # noqa: E402

LEDGER = REPO_ROOT / "references" / "project-standards.md"
DR_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "decisions"

# The grammar and normalisation are ONE home, scripts/dbcore.py (rule 5): this script and
# scripts/db.py's dispose-adversarial-finding (OWNER-RULED) both anchor on the same
**Seed 1.**
```
SUPERSEDES: decisions/DR-2026-08-19-research-restart-operative-instrument.md :: "the junction rows and the count must agree exactly"
  BY: references/project-standards.md :: "`search_executions.results_admitted` IS RAISE-ONLY AFTER INSERT."
```
The target sentence (DR-2026-08-19 §12.1 step 7) described `results_admitted` as bound to agree
exactly with the admission edges at every point after insert. The owner's 2026-09-26 ruling above
holds instead that the count is raise-only after insert: an admission edge added later
(`link-admission`) raises it to `max(count, edges)`, and removing one (`unlink-admission`) lowers

25	| 087 | PARTLY | Writer scope confirmed; candidate `harm_finding` re-opens GAP-059 (CLOSED-DECIDED); `contested` has no reader; value/unit/empty-setting is ruled (OR-3, T-1b step 8); lens re-key is gated by OR-1c |

41	
42	Found in the two session records, passes 8 and 9, and the diffs of PRs #211/#212 (`git log origin/main..HEAD`, `git show`). Each is referenced from the gap it affects.
43	
44	- **U1. No determination is possible on any parameter these batches fed.** `base_parameters.accessibility_direction` is NULL on parameters 4 to 11 (`select parameter_id, accessibility_direction from base_parameters`); `compose_value` returns no interval when the direction is None (`scripts/assess/assess_cell.py:902`). So GAP-074's "consequence", GAP-094's "re-run the determination" and any synthesis on these rows are blocked before units or terms matter. The writer exists (`db.py set-parameter-direction`, `scripts/db.py:1558`); the held text states directions (REF-00468, ext 193: "would have to be increased to 2500 mm ... to accommodate our entire study sample"). Research-data work, no tooling.
45	- **U2. OR-1 ACTION (2) is unmet on every row of both batches.** "Fill every relevant model on a determination and on the figures under it; do not read the CHECK's 'at least one' as the aim" (`references/project-standards.md`, Owner rulings 2026-10-29). Identity only, ICF and needs NULL: `select created_by_session, count(*), sum(icf_code is not null), sum(needs_code is not null) from source_value_extractions where created_by_session like 'session_2026-11-06%' group by 1` → (batch, 25, 0, 0), (batch-2, 35, 0, 0). Gated by OR-1c (open on `governance/owner-browser.yaml`, `gates: true`) and workplan D-2/T-3.
46	- **U3. The reading ledger counts a pre-screen as a full reading.** `v_scan_ledger` (`scripts/migrations/114_extraction_slug_and_root.sql:231`) gives READ-NOTHING-FOUND whenever `text_scope = 'full'`, whatever `method`. `scan_debt.py` treats READ-NOTHING-FOUND as paid. So the two batches discharged scan debt (`scan_debt.py` DEBT 477 on `MAIN`, 457 on `BRANCH`) on readings whose absence claims the critic disproved twice (findings 143, 144, 161, 162, 167, 168).
47	- **U4. GAP-078's remedy ignores OR-16 and names a held source.** OR-16: "read what we hold first". 47 held sources are NOT-READ for parameters 7 and 10: `select parameter_id, status, count(*) from v_scan_ledger where parameter_id in (7,10) group by 1,2`. The stash also holds room-acoustics leads from batch 01, three claimed Co-1 (`select ref_id, tier_claimed, substr(title,1,60) from source_locators where ref_id between 'REF-00965' and 'REF-00970'`); batch 01 is the batch whose co-authors were fabricated (CLAUDE.md §5(c)), so any re-admission needs `--verify-authors`.
48	- **U5. None of the four owner decisions is on the owner's page.** 2026-10-28 (second), ACTION (1): "Put every decision to the owner as a prompt with its full context and its options, never as a bare row". `grep -n 'REF-00468\|England\|GAP-07' governance/owner-browser.yaml` → nothing.
49	- **U6. GAP-074 does not cite GAP-068** (parameter 5 "may name a space, not a quantity ... a diameter or an area"), which is the same question. The report states square spaces for the 360-degree turn (160 × 160, 210 × 210, 250 × 250 cm, PDF page 103 and 166) beside diameters (ext 193, 2500 mm). Not filed, not in GAP-082.
50	- **U7. The sub-national class is wider than England.** REF-00995 (Flemish decree) is `BE`, REF-01013 (Ontario Building Code) is `CA`, REF-01029 (CERMI Comunidad de Madrid) is `ES`: `select ref_id, jurisdiction, substr(pub_title,1,60) from evidence_sources where ref_id in ('REF-00995','REF-01013','REF-01029')`. `JurisdictionCode` has no sub-national member (`python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from schemas.enums import JurisdictionCode as J;print([m.value for m in J if '-' in m.value])"` → []).
51	- **U8. Four passes are open, not one.** `select pass_id, closed_at from adversarial_passes where closed_at is null` → 1, 2, 5, 7. Passes 1 and 2 are held open by ruling/plan (`scripts/db.py:4553` docstring). **Pass 5** (subject `session_2026-10-16-r29-compensating-revert`) has 11 SUSTAINED findings with no disposition (`select verdict, disposition, count(*) from adversarial_findings where pass_id=5 group by 1,2`), no session record under `sessions/` (`ls sessions | grep 2026-10-16` → nothing) and no gap (`select gap_id from gaps where description like '%r29%' or description like '%pass 5%'` → none).
52	- **U9. Typed columns contradict their own notes.** `tier_guess` is 1 on candidates 150 and 152 (`select candidate_id, tier_guess from search_candidates where candidate_id in (150,152)`), while their notes say "Tier guess 3, not 1". `search_executions.results_found` is 15 on exec 201 while its note says 17. All three candidates carry a "RESOLVED ... by session" marker while `disposition` is still `PENDING-VERIFICATION`: `resolve-candidate` was used as a note channel, which reads as a resolution.
53	- **U10. REF-00044's DOI is answerable from held payloads.** Its title string embeds `10.1080/10400430903496580` and its `doi` column is NULL; no held payload carries that DOI (`git grep -l 10400430903496580 -- retrieval-log` → none); PubMed's record (`retrieval-log/session_2026-11-06-pipeline-batch/edb5140e7b6d9611.xml`) and a Crossref-deposited reference list (`retrieval-log/session_2026-09-01-research-batch-04-accessible-circulation/crossref_10.3141_2145-08.json`, "Steinfeld E., Maisel J., Feathers D., and D'…") both give `10.1080/10400430903520280`. **Written:** 2026-11-06, read-only, against branch `ccr-f9662223-3a0e7g` (PR #212) at `5179025`, schema `user_version` 116 (`python3 -c "import sqlite3;print(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True).execute('pragma user_version').fetchone())"`).
**Nothing here is a ruling or an implementation.** Every figure carries the command that computes it; re-run it rather than trust the figure (CLAUDE.md rule 7a). `MAIN` below is `git show origin/main:data/guidebook.db` copied to a read-only scratch file; `BRANCH` is `data/guidebook.db`.

---

## 0. Summary of verdicts

| Gap | Verdict | One line |
|---|---|---|
| 074 | CONFIRMED | Term undefined; misses GAP-068 and the missing direction on parameter 5 |
| 075 | PARTLY | Derivation gap real; "clinical would misstate the source" is contradicted by `governance/evidence-methodology.md:43`; the writer to reclassify already exists |
| 076 | PARTLY | Inconsistency real; "nothing rules the convention" is wrong: OR-1, OR-1b rule the consequences, OR-1c (open) is the gate; ICF and needs lenses are empty on every row, which the gap misses |
| 077 | PARTLY | Real, and wider than England: Flanders, Ontario, Madrid sources carry the national code |
| 078 | PARTLY | Zero rows true; remedy contradicts OR-16 and names a source already held |
| 079 | CONFIRMED | Same structure as GAP-049 (R1 passes on a targeted search with no source) |
| 080 | PARTLY | `tier_guess` columns still read 1 on 150 and 152; the DOI question is answerable from held payloads; admission of 151 is blocked by GAP-008/GAP-030 |
| 081 | CONFIRMED | The wrong page range is still on the `citation_mining` row; `pages` convention duplicates GAP-043(2) |
| 082 | PARTLY | One stated reason is false (the 210 cm sentence is whole on PDF page 167); the 360-degree square spaces (PDF page 103) are omitted from the list |
| 083 | CONFIRMED | |
| 084 | CONFIRMED | |
| 085 | PARTLY | Understated: every scan row in the database is `pre-screen`, and `v_scan_ledger` counts them as full readings (root cause not recorded) |
| 086 | PARTLY | `R16-scan` does read `source_scans`; three registered checks read `source_value_extractions`; one proposed rule already exists; the real residual is gate-time `claim_text` re-verification |
| 087 | PARTLY | Writer scope confirmed; candidate `harm_finding` re-opens GAP-059 (CLOSED-DECIDED); `contested` has no reader; value/unit/empty-setting is ruled (OR-3, T-1b step 8); lens re-key is gated by OR-1c |
| 088 | PARTLY | Mechanism confirmed; it is the ratified DR-2026-09-26 §2.2(b) refusal; the WebSearch half duplicates GAP-034 |
| 089 | PARTLY | `pages_read` = pages held is documented design; the defect is in `v_scan_ledger` |
| 090 | WRONG | The full Korean sentences verify; the quotes were truncated by the operator |
| 091 | PARTLY | A sanctioned two-step path exists; the proposed "targets with adversarial-pass" contradicts the owner's OQ-7 answer |
| 092 | PARTLY | Misses confirmed; same root cause as 085; a figure inventory is new apparatus with a cheaper alternative |
| 093 | PARTLY | Code confirmed; the overwritten values were NULL, so nothing was lost; finding 184 SURVIVED it as designed |
| 094 | PARTLY | Length mixing confirmed; force half WRONG (parameter 6 holds only N); duplicates GAP-072 and ruled workplan item T-1b step 9 |
| 095 | PARTLY | G01/G02 root cause found; all six advisory checks are red on `MAIN` too (none new); `scan_debt` is red by design |
| 096 | PARTLY | Passes 1, 2 and 5 are open as well; disposing finding 140 cannot unblock closure |

Counts (`grep -c` over the table above): CONFIRMED 5, PARTLY 17, WRONG 1.

---

## 1. Issues the author did not record

Found in the two session records, passes 8 and 9, and the diffs of PRs #211/#212 (`git log origin/main..HEAD`, `git show`). Each is referenced from the gap it affects.

- **U1. No determination is possible on any parameter these batches fed.** `base_parameters.accessibility_direction` is NULL on parameters 4 to 11 (`select parameter_id, accessibility_direction from base_parameters`); `compose_value` returns no interval when the direction is None (`scripts/assess/assess_cell.py:902`). So GAP-074's "consequence", GAP-094's "re-run the determination" and any synthesis on these rows are blocked before units or terms matter. The writer exists (`db.py set-parameter-direction`, `scripts/db.py:1558`); the held text states directions (REF-00468, ext 193: "would have to be increased to 2500 mm ... to accommodate our entire study sample"). Research-data work, no tooling.
- **U2. OR-1 ACTION (2) is unmet on every row of both batches.** "Fill every relevant model on a determination and on the figures under it; do not read the CHECK's 'at least one' as the aim" (`references/project-standards.md`, Owner rulings 2026-10-29). Identity only, ICF and needs NULL: `select created_by_session, count(*), sum(icf_code is not null), sum(needs_code is not null) from source_value_extractions where created_by_session like 'session_2026-11-06%' group by 1` → (batch, 25, 0, 0), (batch-2, 35, 0, 0). Corpus-wide `select count(*), sum(icf_code is not null), sum(needs_code is not null) from source_value_extractions` → (214, 1, 3). Gated by OR-1c (open on `governance/owner-browser.yaml`, `gates: true`) and workplan D-2/T-3.
- **U3. The reading ledger counts a pre-screen as a full reading.** `v_scan_ledger` (`scripts/migrations/114_extraction_slug_and_root.sql:231`) gives READ-NOTHING-FOUND whenever `text_scope = 'full'`, whatever `method`. `scan_debt.py` treats READ-NOTHING-FOUND as paid. Every scan row in the database is `pre-screen` with `open_pass_done = 0`: `select method, count(*), sum(open_pass_done) from source_scans group by 1` → ('pre-screen', 18, 0). `select status, method, count(*) from v_scan_ledger group by 1,2` → READ-NOTHING-FOUND/pre-screen 9 on `MAIN`, 22 on `BRANCH`. So the two batches discharged scan debt (`scan_debt.py` DEBT 477 on `MAIN`, 457 on `BRANCH`) on readings whose absence claims the critic disproved twice (findings 143, 144, 161, 162, 167, 168).
- **U4. GAP-078's remedy ignores OR-16 and names a held source.** OR-16: "read what we hold first". 47 held sources are NOT-READ for parameters 7 and 10: `select parameter_id, status, count(*) from v_scan_ledger where parameter_id in (7,10) group by 1,2`. The Irish TGD M 2022 the gap proposes to fetch is held with text (REF-01018; `grep -h '"ref_id": "REF-01018"' retrieval-log/*/manifest.jsonl`), as are REF-01015 (TGD M) and REF-01014 (ISO/CD 21542). The stash also holds room-acoustics leads from batch 01, three claimed Co-1 (`select ref_id, tier_claimed, substr(title,1,60) from source_locators where ref_id between 'REF-00965' and 'REF-00970'`); batch 01 is the batch whose co-authors were fabricated (CLAUDE.md §5(c)), so any re-admission needs `--verify-authors`.
- **U5. None of the four owner decisions is on the owner's page.** 2026-10-28 (second), ACTION (1): "Put every decision to the owner as a prompt with its full context and its options, never as a bare row". `grep -n 'REF-00468\|England\|GAP-07' governance/owner-browser.yaml` → nothing.
- **U6. GAP-074 does not cite GAP-068** (parameter 5 "may name a space, not a quantity ... a diameter or an area"), which is the same question. The report states square spaces for the 360-degree turn (160 × 160, 210 × 210, 250 × 250 cm, PDF page 103 and 166) beside diameters (ext 193, 2500 mm). Not filed, not in GAP-082.
- **U7. The sub-national class is wider than England.** REF-00995 (Flemish decree) is `BE`, REF-01013 (Ontario Building Code) is `CA`, REF-01029 (CERMI Comunidad de Madrid) is `ES`: `select ref_id, jurisdiction, substr(pub_title,1,60) from evidence_sources where ref_id in ('REF-00995','REF-01013','REF-01029')`. `JurisdictionCode` has no sub-national member (`python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from schemas.enums import JurisdictionCode as J;print([m.value for m in J if '-' in m.value])"` → []).
- **U8. Four passes are open, not one.** `select pass_id, closed_at from adversarial_passes where closed_at is null` → 1, 2, 5, 7. Passes 1 and 2 are held open by ruling/plan (`scripts/db.py:4553` docstring). **Pass 5** (subject `session_2026-10-16-r29-compensating-revert`) has 11 SUSTAINED findings with no disposition (`select verdict, disposition, count(*) from adversarial_findings where pass_id=5 group by 1,2`), no session record under `sessions/` (`ls sessions | grep 2026-10-16` → nothing) and no gap (`select gap_id from gaps where description like '%r29%' or description like '%pass 5%'` → none).
- **U9. Typed columns contradict their own notes.** `tier_guess` is 1 on candidates 150 and 152 (`select candidate_id, tier_guess from search_candidates where candidate_id in (150,152)`), while their notes say "Tier guess 3, not 1". `search_executions.results_found` is 15 on exec 201 while its note says 17. All three candidates carry a "RESOLVED ... by session" marker while `disposition` is still `PENDING-VERIFICATION`: `resolve-candidate` was used as a note channel, which reads as a resolution.
- **U10. REF-00044's DOI is answerable from held payloads.** Its title string embeds `10.1080/10400430903496580` and its `doi` column is NULL; no held payload carries that DOI (`git grep -l 10400430903496580 -- retrieval-log` → none); PubMed's record (`retrieval-log/session_2026-11-06-pipeline-batch/edb5140e7b6d9611.xml`) and a Crossref-deposited reference list (`retrieval-log/session_2026-09-01-research-batch-04-accessible-circulation/crossref_10.3141_2145-08.json`, "Steinfeld E., Maisel J., Feathers D., and D'…") both give `10.1080/10400430903520280`. That DOI is on REF-00059 and REF-00192, so add-source would refuse an admission of candidate 151 under R9 until GAP-030's `correct-locator` exists.
- **U11. The `citation_mining` deferral row still states the wrong page range** ("PDF pages 159-173"; `select deferred_reason from citation_mining where local_ref_id='AWM-01'`) and carries `backward = 1, forward = 1` on a deferral (GAP-021's behaviour, decided by GAP-022). The correction is only in scan 15.
- **U12. A 271,499-byte duplicate is committed.** `scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-pipeline-batch-2/awm.txt` is byte-identical to `retrieval-log/session_2026-11-06-pipeline-batch-2/e664fb2f8174f4f8-full-text.txt` (`sha256sum` both → `bae3334434e4025d…`). Rule 5 in spirit; delete in the next commit.
- **U13. Pass 8's harm finding names a column with no meaning.** Finding 142 attacks `contested = 0` on ext 183, and both session records repeat that "no writer changes that column". `source_value_extractions.contested` has no reader: no view (`select name from sqlite_master where type='view' and sql like '%contested%'` → none), no script outside the writer (`git grep -n 'contested' -- scripts schemas | grep -v migrations`; only `scripts/db.py:1921` and `:2949`). Its last reader was a view in `scripts/migrations/057_baseline_2026-08-12.sql:6809`.

---
